### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/lint/score.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/lint/score.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 48 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0616c3001ae4cdb31819220d1dd60371472758f0` — the merge of head `ca353ccee80626d8346b6e19fc46801095e92fec` into base `5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0616c3001ae4cdb31819220d1dd60371472758f0 && git checkout 0616c3001ae4cdb31819220d1dd60371472758f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3 ca353ccee80626d8346b6e19fc46801095e92fec && git checkout -B drift-repro 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3 && git merge --no-ff ca353ccee80626d8346b6e19fc46801095e92fec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5ff858b798c5f68ad8910729c65bb6bdca4844f3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Full first-round review of this head; no earlier record or claim stood on the PR or on card 35926. Claim: comment 7138336858. Read-only shape: the diff `57445a69981..5874e77554e`, the card, and the head's check-runs (61 success, 9 expected skips, 0 failed, 0 pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Both booleans read as absent at every reader**, re-derived on the head tree, not taken from the PR body: `MetadataProvider.tsx:781` passes only `'grid'` / `'form'` to `resolveInlineMode` and anything else as `undefined`; `resolveInlineMode` (`deriveMasterDetail.ts`) returns the value only when it is one of the two strings and otherwise takes the shape default; `formFactorOf` (`validate-field-consumers.ts:1278`) does the same. No server package reads the value: `driver-sql/builtin-column-collision.ts` and `metadata-core/object-schema-fls-references.ts` only name the key in classification tables. The three reader files are byte-identical between the merge base and `origin/main` b01d8f97e97.
- **So the D2 delete is lossless**, for `true` and for `false`. Retiring `false` goes past the card's title (which names `true` only); it is the same key under the same ADR-0049 reasoning and the PR body states it. A `false` does not opt a child out of a parent field group either: the reader passes it as `undefined`, so nothing it did is lost.
- **The refusal is real at both channels**: `z.enum(['grid','form'], { error })` returns the prescription only for a boolean input and leaves every other input to zod; `field-inline-edit-boolean.pin.test.ts` asserts issue code `invalid_value`, path `inlineEdit` and the message for both booleans, the two controls, an unknown string, and a `@ts-expect-error` on a typed boolean.
- **Data at rest**: the conversion walks `objects[]` and `objectExtensions[]` field maps, guarded on `typeof === 'boolean'`, idempotent, fixture covers both collections and both ride-through values. A stored `object_extension` row reaches it through `STORED_ONLY_COLLECTIONS` in `stored.ts`. The standalone `field` metadata type has no stack collection and passes through `applyConversionsToStoredItem` unchanged; that is the same reach as every earlier field-level conversion (`field-malformed-scale-precision-removed`), not a gap this diff opens.
- **Version text**: `packages/spec/package.json` is 18.6.0 on the head and on `origin/main` b01d8f97e97, the changeset is `minor`, the message says 18.7.0 and `retiredAfter` is `'18.6.0'`; the JOIN row in `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` holds that together if a release lands first.
- **Order slots**: conversion order 84 and rationale order 124 are free on the head and on `origin/main` b01d8f97e97 (highest there: 83 and 123).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct spelling. The value answers whether the diff widens an accept set or enlarges the public surface; a narrowing answers `no` and carries the `(narrowing)` arm, which is the breaking marker (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; `clause2-line.mjs`). The diff widens nothing: no public export moves (no `api-surface` snapshot in the diff), the new form row and translation keys are not an accept set. The line is line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right (a value refused), and `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is the level that kind takes. The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM / TO table, the one-line fix and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered field-inline-edit-boolean-removed, field-inline-edit-boolean-retired`). No tombstone is owed: the key stays, a value leaves, on the `indexes[].unique: true` error-map precedent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` 1 (who writes the PR body): answered, the seat applied the prepared body; it reads at this head. Question 2 (signature line 1, closing line 2): answered, kept; the first-line reader reads the card relation.
- Dev flag, `check:platform-checklist` red on main: **verified unrelated.** At the merge base 57445a69981, `access-security.json:1883` anchors `packages/metadata-core/src/anonymous-form-intake.ts#anonymousFormExplicitWithdrawals` and that file declares the symbol 0 times (it lives in `packages/spec/src/ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts`). `origin/main` b01d8f97e97 re-pointed the anchor, and the gate exits 0 there (1763/1773 anchors resolved, the 10 on its named residual). This diff touches neither file.
- Dev flag, skills text: finding S1 below.
- Dev flag, `scenario-tags.ts`: finding S2 below.
- Dev flag, sister repos not measured: escalated to the seat. An authored boolean in hotcrm or cloud meets `tsc` and the parse on their next spec bump; the changeset carries the fix and `os migrate meta --from 17 --write` applies it. Not a defect of this diff.
- SQL push-down: no query code in the diff.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

- `field.zod.ts`: the narrowing takes no capability away at a consumer; it makes the vocabulary equal to what the readers honour since the field-group ruling (record 7046311205). The `.describe()` and TSDoc that ship in `src/**/*.zod.ts` are true after the change, and the `relatedList` prose no longer calls itself the mirror of a key that changed meaning. The refusal text carries no tracker number.
- `field-inline-edit-boolean-removed.ts`, `registry.ts`: agrees with the contract above; `retiredFromLoadPath: true` is the right arm for a value a live author must be told about and a stored row must not trip on.
- `18.field-inline-edit-boolean-retired.ts`: states the one judgment the conversion cannot make (whether the author meant the child inlined, which only a parent field group does). Accurate against `related-list-body-table.ts` and the readers.
- `field.form.ts` with the reconciliation ledger: offering the key as a Grid / Form select is the consequence the ledger test prescribes once its ruled reason (no widget spells the union) stops being true; the gate `data.type in ['lookup','master_detail']` matches the sibling relationship rows.
- `registry.ts.template`: the fragment is accurate. See N1.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix, carried by a card, release-coupled).** The published skills teach the value this parse refuses: on `origin/main` b01d8f97e97, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md:285` reads `inlineEdit: true // auto ... (default)`, and `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json:439` expects "`true` or absent picks by the child's shape". It cannot be fixed in this PR: `skills/**` is a governed surface, the card excludes skills text, and the `Skills-docs:` rule sends a PR outside the skills lane to `follow-up #N`. The earlier skills card 35902 is closed and does not carry it. `@objectstack/skills` versions in the same fixed changeset group as `@objectstack/spec`, so the follow-up has to land before the release that publishes this narrowing, or one release ships a skill and a parser that disagree. Closes when the card is filed and the `Skills-docs:` line reads `follow-up #N`.
- **S2 (should-fix, carried by a card for the eval lane).** `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-tags.ts:493-500` (`records-forms.master-detail-inline-edit`) credits `inlineEdit === true`, `'grid'` or `'form'` on the raw field as "edited inline on its master". Since the field-group ruling none of the three inlines anything without a parent field group, and after this PR `true` is refused at parse. The tag needs re-specifying against `fieldGroups[].relatedList`, which changes scores and is the eval lane's decision, not a one-token delete here. No open card names it.
- **N1 (nit).** The new step-18 rationale fragment names `objectstack#35889`. `os migrate meta` prints the rationale to an author (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:985`), who has no tracker. `check:doc-authoring` does not reach this text and one landed fragment does the same, so it is not a gate failure; the words "the maintainer's field-group ruling" stand without the number.
- **N2 (nit).** Untyped fixtures still spell a field-level boolean: `MetadataProvider.merge.test.ts:311,380,386`, `MetadataProvider.composedObjectsIdentity-11699.test.tsx:87`, `deriveRelatedLists.relatedListsOrder-27069.test.ts:142,156`. They pin reader tolerance of unparsed input; harmless, and no text scan can tell them from the live view-level key.
- **N3 (nit).** `resolveInlineMode` still types its parameter `boolean | InlineMode | undefined` and its comment still says "`true` / undefined".

No must-fix on the contract faces. Not a contract finding, for the seat: GitHub reports this head `mergeable_state: dirty` against `origin/main` b01d8f97e97 (one content conflict, the count pin in `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`). The head has to move by a main merge, which is neither a pure regeneration nor prose-only, so the merged head owes a delta read of this record.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head 5874e77554e0abbf259bd2d15f9b59f029bd7b1b

The substance is accepted: the contract review of this head is PASS (comment 7138399935) and nothing below asks for a design change. The head cannot land as it stands, and one declaration line is still in its pre-ACCEPT spelling, so the verdict is REWORK with three mechanical items.

**Must-fix**

1. **Merge `origin/main`; this head conflicts.** GitHub reports `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty` against `origin/main` b01d8f97e97. One content conflict: the count pin in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts` (main reads 823 since the Studio list columns change; this branch reads 772). Merge through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`, regenerate the i18n bundles (`node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`), and write the pin from the measured count with its comment line, not from arithmetic. Then the scoped re-checks, and, because the PR declares a narrowing, the full dogfood battery again on the final head with `dogfood_battery` pinned to it.
2. **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed` becomes `follow-up #N`.** The seat files the owed card (skills lane) and rewrites the PR body line; the dev rewrites the same line in `.changeset/35926-field-inline-edit-boolean-retired.md` in the push for item 1. The card names both sites on `origin/main` b01d8f97e97, not only the one the line lists: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md:285` (`inlineEdit: true // auto`) and `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json:439` ("`true` or absent picks by the child's shape"). It is release-coupled: `@objectstack/skills` is in the same fixed changeset group as `@objectstack/spec`, so it lands before the release that publishes this narrowing. Card 35902, which the claim pointed at for skills text, is closed and does not carry this.
3. **Add `'@objectstack/lint': patch` to the changeset frontmatter.** `packages/lint` is `private: false` and the diff touches `src/validate-field-consumers.ts`; the checklist's test is the touched published package, not the size of the change. For the record, the edit is comment text on two unexported functions and ships no byte: on a built tree (fad5ea01bf8) `function formFactorOf` is in `dist/index.js` once and its doc comment zero times, in `.js` and `.d.ts` alike. One body sentence saying so is enough.

**The six checks**

- **Shape.** Open, draft, base `main`, 49 files, +524 / -70, no `content/docs/releases/` path, no governed path (`skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**` untouched), one non-empty changeset, no one-shot script in the diff. `Fixes` is right: the card's acceptance (the boolean follows a retirement route, every playbook gate green) is delivered whole. Declarations read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the spelling is correct for a narrowing.
- **Premise, measured.** Re-read on the head tree: `MetadataProvider.tsx:781`, `resolveInlineMode` and `formFactorOf` pass a boolean as absent; no server package reads the value. Consumer sweep for the old stance: every remaining `inlineEdit: true` / `false` under `examples/`, `packages/lint/src/showcase-shape.fixtures.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol` and `ui/` list, gantt and detail code is the view-level or component-level key, which is live and unchanged; the field-level leftovers are six untyped test fixtures (contract review N2).
- **Gates, check-runs at this head.** 61 success, 9 expected skips, 0 unexpected skips, 0 failed, 0 pending; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both `success`. `dogfood_battery` in report 7138019330 is pinned to the full head sha, full battery, exit 0, 487 files and 4127 tests passed, none failed. The refusal pins assert issue code, path and message, not a bare failure. `check:platform-checklist` is unrelated: red at the merge base 57445a69981 on an `access-security.json` anchor naming a file that does not declare the symbol, repaired on `origin/main` b01d8f97e97, where the gate exits 0; this diff touches neither file.
- **Accepted deviations.** The whole boolean arm is retired, not only `true` as the card's title says: `false` reads as absent at the same readers. The field form gains an `inlineEdit` select because the ledger test prescribes it once the union is gone. Files past the claim's listed surface are each a direct consequence and are named in the PR body (the form row and its reconciliation ledger, the translation bundles and count pin, the migration rationale fragment, cli and lint count pins, one app-shell test). Seven locales carry the new label as source text. The report shows no API read that git could have answered (`mcp_calls` 0).
- **Out-of-scope findings and `Skills-docs:`.** Skills text: item 2. `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-tags.ts:493-500` credits `inlineEdit === true` (and either form factor) as "edited inline" with no parent field group: a card for the eval lane, filed by the seat, not changed here. Sister repos (hotcrm, cloud) are unmeasured: an authored boolean there meets `tsc` and the parse on the next spec bump, and the changeset carries the fix; the seat decides whether a cross-repo note is owed. `docs/adr/0035` keeps `inlineEdit: true` as history, governed, untouched.
- **Landing clause.** A declared narrowing: it waits for the maintainer's approval and no seat readies, arms or queues it on green. After items 1 to 3 the merged head owes its own check-runs reading, the pinned dogfood battery, a delta read of contract review 7138399935, and a fresh record here.

Sentences read one by one. Changeset: the summary line, the three FROM / TO rows, the one-line fix (`os migrate meta --from 17 --write`), "The view-level `inlineEdit` ... is a different key and is unchanged", and the three kit bullets (spec, field form, cli corpus) each match the diff. Docs: `field-types.mdx` (the property row, the example now `'grid'`, "or no `inlineEdit` resolving to the grid", "Without `inlineEdit` the form factor is picked from the child"), `fields.mdx` (example and row, "a boolean is refused at parse"), `common-patterns.mdx` (example), `flows.mdx` ("the children a field group of the object places"). The four `content/docs/references/**` pages are generated and match the new `.describe()` text.

Delta read of contract review 7138399935 (PASS at head 5874e77554e), which said the merged head owes one. Claim: comment 7144213273. That round left should-fix findings, so the follow-up head is read as a delta by the same reviewing session; this run is a fresh one-shot sub-agent of it and re-measured what it carries over instead of trusting it. Read-only shape: the range `5874e77554e..ca353ccee80` (merge commit f671e98ad2f onto `origin/main` bfd1049f22f, then one changeset commit), the card, the dev report 7144059566, and the head's check-runs (61 success, 9 expected skips, 0 failed, 0 pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moved, measured per file.** The PR's file list is the same 49 paths before and after the merge. Comparing each file's patch against its own merge base (`57445a69981..5874e77554e` against `bfd1049f22f..ca353ccee80`), 47 of 49 are identical by patch id. The two that differ are the changeset (prose face, read by the seat) and the count pin test. So the delta on the contract faces is one test file.
- **The earlier derivation still stands on the merged tree.** Between the old merge base and `origin/main` eec6fb3f002, main changed none of: `field.zod.ts`, `field.form.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/**`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/**`, `liveness/field.json`, `validate-field-consumers.ts`, `MetadataProvider.tsx`, `deriveMasterDetail.ts`. The readers that pass a boolean as absent are the bytes the first record read.
- **Main brought no new author of the retired value into code.** In the whole main range the only added line that spells `inlineEdit` is in `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` (finding S1 below, already carried by a card).

## 维护者速读
- 用户可感：在主从或查找字段上把「内联编辑」写成真或假时，校验会直接报错并给出改法；已存的旧定义在启动和迁移时会自动去掉这个值，页面表现不变。字段设计器多了一个「表格 / 表单」下拉框。
- 为什么做：你裁定「一律只看分组」之后，子表要不要显示在父表单里，只由父对象的字段分组决定。这两个真假值和不写完全一样，写了也没用。
- 出错会怎样：最坏情况是有人在源码里还写着真假值，升级后校验报错，并看到改法；已存数据会自动转换，不会坏页面。技能文档里还有一处教旧写法，已另立卡 #37042，须在同一个版本发布前合入。
- 要你做什么：这是申报的收窄（破坏性变更），需要你批准后才能合入。
